title: GDT Tagged Summary
description: The structured summary a GDT-conformant tagger emits for a single SQL query/model.

operations.description: Keys are GDT category names; each value is an array of occurrences (empty array if the category is absent).

source_columns.description: Column names referenced anywhere in the computed expression (every exp.Column found in that subtree). Omitted or empty if the expression references no columns (e.g. a literal-only expression).

aggregate.description: One entry per aggregate function call (exp.Sum, exp.Count, exp.Avg, exp.Min, exp.Max, ...), not one entry per GROUP BY clause. group_by_keys is repeated on every aggregate belonging to the same query.

function.description: Aggregate function name, lowercased, e.g. sum, count, avg, min, max

argument_summary.description: Summary of the aggregated expression, e.g. 'amount', 'customer_id', '*'

output.description: Output column alias, if the aggregate is aliased

distinct.description: True for e.g. COUNT(DISTINCT x) — exp.Distinct wrapping the argument

group_by_keys.description: Summaries of the query's GROUP BY expressions (exp.Group.expressions); empty/absent if the aggregate has no GROUP BY (e.g. a bare scalar aggregate)

source_columns.description: Column names referenced in the aggregated argument expression. Omitted or empty for COUNT(*) (no column argument).

function.description: The windowed function, e.g. row_number, rank, lag, lead, sum, avg

order_by.description: Summaries of ORDER BY expressions within the OVER clause (exp.Window.order)

frame.description: Frame spec (exp.WindowSpec), if the OVER clause defines one

source_columns.description: Column names referenced in the windowed function's own argument (e.g. 'amount' in SUM(amount) OVER (...)). Does not include partition_by/order_by columns — those are already structured separately.

cast.description: One entry per exp.Cast (type coercion only — not date/number formatting functions).

source_summary.description: Summary of the expression being cast (exp.Cast.this)

target_type.description: Target data type, lowercased, e.g. varchar, int, timestamp (exp.Cast.to)

output.description: Output column alias, if the cast is aliased

safe.description: True for a safe/non-throwing cast variant (e.g. TRY_CAST, SAFE_CAST)

source_columns.description: Column names referenced in the expression being cast (exp.Cast.this) — usually one, more if it's a compound expression like CAST(a + b AS int).

conditional.description: One entry per exp.Case (CASE/WHEN — including dialect-specific single-branch forms like IFF/IF that a tagger normalizes onto this same shape; see docs/decisions.md). Emitted for every occurrence found anywhere in the query, independent of whether the same node is also covered by a compute entry — see docs/grammar.md.

output.description: Output column alias, if the conditional expression is the top-level aliased value

operand_summary.description: For simple CASE <expr> WHEN ... form, the compared expression (exp.Case.this); absent for searched CASE WHEN <bool> form

default.description: The ELSE expression summary (exp.Case.default), if present

subquery_cte.description: One entry per exp.CTE or exp.Subquery — a structural complexity signal, not itself a transformation; can co-occur with any other category.

kind.description: cte for a WITH-clause entry (exp.CTE), subquery for an inline derived table (exp.Subquery)

alias.description: The CTE/subquery alias name, if present

location.description: Where it's referenced, e.g. from, where, join

wildcard_select.description: One entry per exp.Star found in the SELECT list — a bare SELECT * or a qualified t.* — optionally with a dialect-specific EXCEPT(...) clause. REPLACE(...) is out of scope for v1; see docs/grammar.md.

kind.description: star for a bare SELECT *; qualified_star for t.* / table.*

qualifier.description: Table alias or name, present only for qualified_star

except_columns.description: Column names excluded via a dialect-specific EXCEPT(...) clause (e.g. BigQuery, Snowflake, DuckDB), if present

json_parse.description: One entry per exp.ParseJSON — parsing a string/variant into a JSON-typed value (e.g. Snowflake/BigQuery PARSE_JSON).

safe.description: True for a safe/non-throwing parse variant (e.g. TRY_PARSE_JSON)

source_columns.description: Column names referenced in the parsed expression

json_extract.description: One entry per JSON path extraction — exp.JSONExtract / exp.JSONExtractScalar. Dialect-specific spellings (Postgres ->/->>, Snowflake : colon operator, BigQuery JSON_VALUE/JSON_QUERY) normalize onto this same shape per docs/decisions.md (0001).

scalar.description: True if the extraction returns a scalar (->>, JSON_VALUE, exp.JSONExtractScalar) rather than a nested JSON value (->, JSON_QUERY, exp.JSONExtract)

source_columns.description: Column names referenced in the source JSON expression

unnest.description: One entry per array/semi-structured unnest — exp.Unnest. Dialect-specific table functions (Snowflake LATERAL FLATTEN, Spark LATERAL VIEW EXPLODE) are expected to normalize onto this same shape per docs/decisions.md (0001); see docs/grammar.md for confidence notes on that mapping.

alias.description: Output row alias for the unnested elements, if present

ordinality.description: True if WITH ORDINALITY / an offset-index column is requested (exp.Unnest.offset)

location.description: Where it's referenced, e.g. from, join

source_columns.description: Column names referenced in the unnested expression

ai_function.description: One entry per call to a recognized AI/ML SQL function (e.g. Snowflake Cortex AI_COMPLETE/AI_CLASSIFY, BigQuery ML.GENERATE_TEXT/AI.GENERATE, Databricks ai_query). Unlike every other category, this is NOT grounded in a dedicated sqlglot AST node — sqlglot has no special node for 'this is an AI vendor function,' so detection is function-name-based against a maintained allowlist. See docs/decisions.md (0003) for the reasoning and consequences (allowlist maintenance burden, expected false negatives for unrecognized/renamed functions).

source_columns.description: Column names referenced in the call's arguments

udf.description: One entry per call to an unrecognized/non-builtin function — typically exp.Anonymous in sqlglot. Like ai_function, NOT grounded in a dedicated AST node; see docs/decisions.md (0003). A tagger should check ai_function's allowlist first — an AI function call is tagged ai_function, not udf. False positives are possible for a genuine builtin sqlglot doesn't yet recognize for a given dialect.

function.description: The called function name as written, schema-qualified if present (e.g. 'my_schema.my_udf')

source_columns.description: Column names referenced in the call's arguments

column_hash.description: One entry per call to a hashing function. Mostly grounded in dedicated sqlglot nodes (exp.MD5, exp.SHA, exp.SHA2); dialect-specific hash functions sqlglot has no dedicated class for (e.g. Snowflake HASH(), BigQuery FARM_FINGERPRINT) fall back to function-name matching, same basis as ai_function/udf but as a fallback rather than the primary detection path — see docs/decisions.md (0003).

function.description: Hash function name, lowercased, e.g. md5, sha1, sha256, hash, farm_fingerprint

argument_summary.description: Summary of the expression(s) being hashed

algorithm_bits.description: Bit length if specified, e.g. 256 for SHA2(x, 256)

source_columns.description: Column names referenced in the hashed expression(s)
